use_case.example:
A customer claims they were charged AED 500 for fuel that they didn't use. With RCCMS, you pull up the contract timeline and show:

problem.description: Your staff is calculating fuel charges on paper or calculators. Sometimes they round down to keep the customer happy. Sometimes they forget to add extra mileage charges. solution.title: How RCCMS Eliminates Calculation Errors

capabilities.name: Automatic Fuel Charge Calculation
capabilities.description: The most common source of revenue loss - fully automated
details: Formula: Fuel Charge = Tank Capacity (L) × (Start Fuel % - End Fuel %) / 100 × Price Per Liter
Example: 60L tank, started at 100%, returned at 25%, petrol at AED 4.50/L
System stores tank capacity for each vehicle in master data
Fuel prices configurable per fuel type (petrol, diesel, electric)
Fuel level recorded at pickup and return
Calculation happens automatically on vehicle return
Manual override available for exceptional cases (with audit trail)
No rounding errors - precise to the fils

use_case.example:
Customer rents a Toyota Camry for 8 days with GPS and insurance:

1. Rental Charges:
   - Daily rate: AED 120/day × 8 days = AED 960
   - GPS rental: AED 15/day × 8 days = AED 120
   - Insurance: AED 25/day × 8 days = AED 200
   - Subtotal: AED 1,280

2. Extra Charges on Return:
   - Fuel used: 60L tank, 100% → 40% = 36L × AED 4.50 = AED 162
   - Extra mileage: Drove 2,500 km, allowed 2,000 km (250/day × 8) = 500 km × AED 0.50 = AED 250
   - Late return: 4 hours × AED 50/hour = AED 200
   - Subtotal extra charges: AED 612

3. Final Calculation:
   - Total before VAT: AED 1,892
   - VAT (5%): AED 94.60
   - Grand Total: AED 1,986.60
   - Deposit paid: AED 1,500
   - Balance due: AED 486.60

All calculated in 0.2 seconds. Staff just needs to confirm the odometer and fuel readings.

technical_excellence.title: Not Just Translation - True Internationalization
technical_excellence.explanation:
RCCMS uses i18next, the industry-standard internationalization framework. This means:

- Proper locale handling (en-US, ar-AE)
- Date and number formatting per locale
- Currency formatting (AED shown correctly in both languages)
- Pluralization rules for Arabic (different from English)
- Contextual translations (same word, different meanings)
- Future-ready for additional languages (French, Urdu, Hindi)

This is enterprise-grade internationalization, not a basic translation layer.
